challenge.better_approach: Open flush on LAN_OPS: refused, the server's own comment rules flush is the owning box's act (Law 6). Change only the tester's message: the tester is held by cc_0, and every other far caller of flush would hit the same refusal. Making the far handle answer truthfully in bus_client is the smallest move that fixes every caller.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the far bus process outlives the client, so its ring is not lost when the sealing process dies: true by construction (the ring is in the far process, not this one); whether the far box's beat flushes that ring is a separate question, measured as ring_depth 87 = posted 87 on the Dell bus at 2026-11-12 ~21:00.
challenge.prior_art: Ticket bc0bbfd33a71 did the same for hold: a far reach no longer sends an op the LAN door refuses (cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_far_client_reaches_without_hold.py). This is its sibling for flush.
challenge.real_collision: None: the tester's comment says flush makes the post a store 'rather than a hope' because the ring lived in the sealing process; for a far handle it does not, and the tester is untouched.

answers.falsifier: RED if a far handle's flush() still sends an op outside ('call','stats','verbs'), or raises; or if a local handle's flush() stops sending op flush.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator relayed it from a measured refusal: the tester's seal from akienasus printed "'flush' is not open across the LAN" at cairn/devices/tester/cli.py line 400
answers.how: In cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py, RemoteBus.flush() on a far home (remote_address not None) returns the local flush shape plus far + why naming the box whose process holds the ring, and sends nothing; a local home still sends op flush. Red-first proof with remote.exchange replaced, as test_a_far_client_reaches_without_hold.py does.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (a diagnostic surface may not report a failure that did not happen: the seal's post landed and codemother accepted it, yet the tester printed that the crossings did not fire) and Law 6 (the far box's ring is its own process's to flush; the LAN door refuses flush on that ground, server.py LAN_OPS).
answers.what: A far bus handle's flush() answers without sending an op the LAN door refuses, so a far-box seal that DID reach codemother is no longer reported as a crossing that never fired.

bullets.text: All 12 far-box sealed posts from akienasus today reached codemother and her sealed replies came back accepted:true; only the trailing flush was refused, and the tester then printed that the crossings did not fire.
Dell bus stats read posted 87, ring_depth 87: nothing has flushed since it started. Recorded, not this ticket.

title: A far bus handle's flush() answers without sending an op the LAN door refuses, so a far-box seal that DID reach codemoth
